newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Lockheed JV seen competitive-Russia partner.
newsitem.headline: Lockheed JV seen competitive-Russia partner.

text.p: A joint venture between Russia's Intersputnik and Lockheed Martin International may make life tough for other firms in the international telecommunication market, the head of Intersputnik said on Monday.
"I think leading international telecommunication firms may face difficulties in competing with the new joint venture," Gennady Kudryavstev, Intersputnik general director, told Reuters.

He said Lockheed Martin Intersputnik Ltd (LMI) planned to launch the first Lockheed Martin A2100 satellite on a Russian-made Proton booster in late 1998. LMI is part of U.S. military and aerospace giant Lockheed Martin Corp.
"The probe will provide South East Asia, the Midle East and Russian regions with telecommunications services," he said.

Kudryavtsev said the first LMI board meeting would held in Moscow this month. He declined to say how much money his company had invested in the venture, which Lockheed expects to generate between $300 million and $500 million in annual revenues by 2001.

Intersputnik was established in 1971 by Eastern Europe countries under the supervision of the former Soviet Union and leases Russian-made satellites. --Viktor Anoshkin, Moscow Newsroom, +7095 941 8520
